# SNMPv3 datagrams captured from net-snmp 5.6.2.1 for the `v3` section of trap-vectors.json
# (read by genvectors.py; capture-v3.sh regenerates the file).
#
# Format: <hex datagram> | <kind> | <credential set> | <name>
#   kind          message  = decodes with that user's keys, with its full expectation
#                 rejected = must be refused (a wrong password)
#                 probe    = an engine-ID discovery probe, answered with a Report
#   credential set  one of USERS in genvectors.py: the user name, protocols and passwords the
#                   sender used, so the reference decoder can localize the keys itself.
#
# The traps were sent with
#   snmptrap -m '' -v 3 -e 0x8000000001020304 -u trapuser -l <level> [-a <A> -A <password>]
#            [-x <X> -X <password>] <receiver> 12345 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.3 i 3
# so each carries sysUpTime.0 = 12345, snmpTrapOID.0 = linkDown and ifIndex.3 = 3 under the
# sender's own engine ID 8000000001020304 (boots 0 and time 0: snmptrap keeps no state).
# The probe is the first datagram of `snmpinform -v 3 -u trapuser -l authPriv ...`.

 | message | sha-aes | net-snmp 5.6 snmptrap -v 3 -l authPriv -a SHA -x AES: linkDown
 | message | sha | net-snmp 5.6 snmptrap -v 3 -l authNoPriv -a SHA: linkDown
 | message | md5-des | net-snmp 5.6 snmptrap -v 3 -l authPriv -a MD5 -x DES: linkDown
 | message | none | net-snmp 5.6 snmptrap -v 3 -l noAuthNoPriv: linkDown
 | rejected | sha-aes | net-snmp 5.6 snmptrap -v 3 -l authPriv with the WRONG authentication password
304f0201033011020470094ab2020300ffe30401040201030410300e04000201000201000400040004003025041180001f888016cd170c1b86a96a000000000400a00e020446e2c5420201000201003000 | probe | none | net-snmp 5.6 snmpinform -v 3: the engine ID discovery probe
